title: The affine derived counit induces the ordinary counit on cohomology
statement: Let A, F, G, adj : F ⊣ G, and their two functor comparisons be as in the affine derived-adjunction statement: F has Q ⋙ F ⋙ inclusion ≅ termwise tilde ⋙ Q and G ≅ inclusion ⋙ R(Γ with scalars transported through ΓSpecIso). Use D_QCoh and derived global sections as in [def-pc-derived-category], [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image], and [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology], and ordinary tilde and Γ as in [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction]. For every K in D_QCoh(Spec A) and integer n there exists an isomorphism e : H^n(F(G(K))) ≅ tilde(Γ(H^n(K))) such that H^n(inclusion(adj.counit_K)) = e.hom followed by the ordinary counit tilde(Γ(H^n(K))) → H^n(K).

proof.text: Global sections is a right adjoint, hence commutes with products. Scalar transport through ΓSpecIso is exact and commutes with products. Affine vanishing gives cohomological bound N=1 on quasi-coherent modules. Passing to underlying abelian groups is exact and conservative; the same vanishing bound holds there. Apply the unbounded cohomological bound with b=-1 to the negative truncation. The truncation triangle removes the negative tail in degree zero. Left exactness of sections on the nonnegative truncation identifies degree-zero derived sections with sections of degree-zero cohomology. Shifts give this identification in every degree.

Use the natural exact-tilde cohomology comparison. On a K-injective representative the canonical derived counit is termwise evaluation; naturality of the truncation comparisons identifies its map on cohomology with the ordinary counit. The comparisons for F and G transport this calculation. The localization universal property descends the comparison for F, and uniqueness of right adjoints transports the canonical adjunction to adj. Absorb the induced right-adjoint isomorphism on cohomology into the source comparison e. This gives the displayed equation, with unchanged target.
